title: Provider Router & Config Invalidation
scope: Understand how OpenWorker's ProviderRouter lazily builds, caches, and invalidates provider clients from SecretStore profiles — preventing stale config from causing LLM failures.
env_vars: OW_PROVIDER_* (provider-specific env vars referenced via ${ENV_VAR} in secrets.json)
OW_SECRET_* (secret references resolved at read time)
config_loader: SecretStore.get('provider:{name}') reads profiles from secrets.json (0600), resolves ${ENV_VAR} references at read time from process env + ~/.config/coworker/.env, then build_provider_client() delegates to the registry's build() factory to construct the SDK client. ProviderRouter caches built clients in self._clients dict with threading.Lock, invalidated via invalidate(name=None).

router_design.dispatch: Dispatches by provider: prefix of model string: openai:gpt-4o → OpenAI client, ollama:llama3 → Ollama client, bare gpt-4o → default (openai)
router_design.prefix_stripped: The provider prefix is stripped before delegating to the SDK (which wants bare model name). _bare() (router.py:70) only strips KNOWN provider prefixes — qwen2.5-coder:32b (version tag, not provider) is returned unchanged
router_design.lazy_build: _client_for(model) builds client lazily from SecretStore profile and caches it in self._clients dict
router_design.thread_safe: Uses threading.Lock for client cache access

invalidation.behavior: Drops cached client(s) so the next call rebuilds with fresh config. If name given → pop one; if None → clear all
invalidation.trigger: Config changes (new key, new Ollama URL) call invalidate() so existing engines pick up the change without a rebuild — the engine still holds the same ProviderRouter instance

config_resolution.build_call: build_provider_client(name, profile, self._secrets) delegates to the registry's build() factory
config_resolution.on_use_callback: Optional on_use(provider_name) callable fired when a completion is dispatched — drives Settings pane 'Last used' line. Best-effort: failures never break a model call

secret_store.env_resolution: Values may be ${ENV_VAR} references resolved at read time from process env + ~/.config/coworker/.env
secret_store.interface_only: Interface abstracts the backend — pluggable (file → Keychain/age-later without touching callers)

findings.test_coverage: openworker/tests/test_provider_router.py verifies: (1) _client_for lazy build with cache hit/miss, (2) _bare() strips known provider prefixes only (qwen2.5-coder:32b returned unchanged), (3) invalidate(name) pops a single client from cache, (4) invalidate() with no arg clears all clients, (5) concurrent _client_for calls are thread-safe under threading.Lock, (6) dispatch by provider: prefix routes to correct SDK client, (7) on_use callback fires best-effort without breaking model calls.
failure_modes: Stale client cache: if config changes without invalidate() call, the engine picks up the new ProviderRouter instance on next engine creation — but in-flight completions may use the stale cached client
Provider prefix mismatch: bare model names without a known prefix fall through to 'openai' default — a typo in the model string silently routes to OpenAI

Env-var resolution failure: if ${ENV_VAR} references an unset variable, SecretStore returns the literal string '${ENV_VAR}' — the SDK receives a literal string as api_key, producing an authentication error (not a silent fallback)
findings.gap_vs_kimi: OpenWorker does NOT apply env-var overrides imperatively after config validation (unlike kimi-cli's augment_provider_with_env_vars). The SecretStore resolves ${ENV_VAR} at read time, and ProviderRouter invalidates on config change. No race between validated config and runtime env.

pydantic_ai_2_impl.pattern: AgentDeps + BaseSettings(env_prefix='OW_') for typed config injection — a single validated AppConfig flows into ProviderRouter, with invalidate() to drop stale clients on config change. Eliminates the env-var race that causes LLMs to read stale/guess provider config.
pydantic_ai_2_impl.why_now: ai-factory's LLMs fail because control.py loads model config via os.getenv at module level with no validation — if the env var is stale or missing, the LLM reads wrong config and produces garbage. OpenWorker's ProviderRouter + SecretStore pattern proves that a single validated config object (injected via AgentDeps) with invalidate() on change eliminates this entire failure class.
pydantic_ai_2_impl.harness_gap: factory/infra/control.py:221 caches OpenAIProvider objects in _PROVIDERS_CACHE (built from SystemSettings at module import via _make_providers(), no invalidate()). factory/infra/control.py:550 instantiates CONTROL_SHEET at module level with no reload on config change. factory/infra/http_client.py:141 caches the _orch_http_client singleton, recreated only on event-loop change. When env vars rotate (API key, URL), these caches retain stale config — LLM calls fail with auth errors blamed on the model. Adoption: ProviderRouter with lazy client caching + invalidate() (rebuild OpenAIProvider from validated SystemSettings), AgentDeps injection so tools receive authoritative typed config — no post-hoc env re-read.
